summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with malaise, fever, and concerns for urinary tract infection and left hip ulcer infection. He has a complex history including paraplegia, chronic indwelling Foley catheter, recurrent UTIs, and chronic kidney disease. The catheter balloon was found to be malpositioned, causing frequent dislodgement and contamination. Urine cultures repeatedly showed mixed flora, indicating contamination rather than true infection, so antibiotics were withheld per infectious disease recommendation to avoid resistance. CT imaging showed no evidence of pyelonephritis or osteomyelitis, though chronic hip changes and synovitis were noted. His creatinine increased slightly, attributed to hypovolemia, and improved with IV fluids. The left hip ulcer was assessed by plastics and deemed non-infected. On the morning of discharge, the patient reported coughing up blood, but evaluation revealed no active bleeding, likely due to brown soda discoloration. He was discharged home with plans for urinary diversion surgery, follow-up with urology and plastics, and instructions to seek care if bleeding recurred.
